Sounds amazing. Tall and thinner than most so it fits in cup holders? Nice! Multiple lid options available for purchase? Cool.

Thing is I tried this next to my other bottles and this was by far the worst at keeping drinks cold. Ice melted in 3 hours or less every time I tried, that’s with half a tray of ice cubs + refrigerated water. All others kept the ice solid for at least 6+ hours.

The style of the bottle is a 5. But if it cannot keep ice from melting and drinks cold as long as my other bottles and tumblers? It’s useless to me. May be good for at home when you can constantly refresh ice and drinks. When traveling? It’s not going to work for me and that’s the main reason I got it. I feel very disappointed especially when they send me emails bragging about how they keep drinks colder way longer than others claim to. They don’t they’re the opposite or what they claim to be.

I tried to review it on their site, but couldn’t get it approved so the product has 5 stars there but I wouldn’t trust that star count.

*update* got a different brand and decided to compare how fast they lose their ability to stay cool. This bottle went from 35 degree water to 66.3 in 3.5 hours. While the other bottle took over 24 hours to get that warm.

text_fidelity_a:
TRX All-in-One Suspension Training System: Weight Training, Cardio, Cross Training, Resistance Training. Full Body Workouts for Home, Travel, and Outdoors. Includes Indoor & Outdoor Anchor system The physical therapist at the hospital had me work on hers when I came in. She thinks the TRX system is the bee's knees. When the thearopy was over I bought one.

Importantly note that the physical therapist specifically told me not to get a knock off unless it had a single strap. If the straps were not connected I would lose the balance building part and she said it would hurt me more than help. The TRX was the only one I saw, at the time, that met her criteria.

I love working on it. In my opinion, There are a couple of things to consider. First is that at my age and inflexibility, the lower body work outs are difficult. You have to get your feet in the straps a certain way and sometimes I find it hard to keep the feet in and do the workout.

The next consideration is that it is difficult to use in a closed door. You really need a fair amount of space around you to work out, and I find a closed door is a hindrance.

Overall i must grudgingly admit the physical therapist is right and the TRX system is just about perfect for getting that resistance training which is so important.
text_fidelity_b: TRX All-in-One Suspension Training System: Weight Training, Cardio, Cross Training, Resistance Training. Full Body Workouts for Home, Travel, and Outdoors. Includes Indoor & Outdoor Anchor system

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness Incline Full Motion Rowing Machine Rower with 350 lb Weight Capacity and LCD Monitor I purchased this unit, and it unfortunately arrived at my condo while I was out of town and my return window expired, or I would have returned it. I’m 63 years old, over 6 feet tall, and a large man. I go about 350 and ordered this unit because it will handle my weight, and it is built quite strong. I’m not sure where they got the child in the picture, but the unit just isn’t as big as it looks in the picture. The unit is built fairly strong, but is too low to the ground and too narrow at the base to be safe for large people. And there is no way to really adjust the pull force requirement, which is a lot if you are heavy.
If you are a large person and want to really use this machine, get a piece of plywood that’s at least 8 inches wider and longer than the base, mount 2 4x4s (stacked) to the front, and one 4x4 on the rear. Then mount the unit to the 4x4s and prepare for a real upper body workout. (Raising the front will allow you to get on the thing without the seat sliding downhill while you get on it). Overall, if you are a 20 year old 100 pounder, this is probably a good unit for you. If you are large, or over 30, you should look elsewhere.

So when I saw this yoga core balance board I decided to give it a try.

I cannot and will not recommend it.

First, it arrived undone. There are little holes around the bottom with clips that snap into place to hold the top to the bottom. One was not in at all the another was not even halfway in. We attempted to snap them in, but could not budge them. The surface was therefore off, as you see in one picture, we could pull it easily away.

Second, for something that calls itself non-slip this is completely slippery. We both stood on it with no socks, socks, and shoes and not one felt non-slippery and in fact we had to hold onto one another and a hard, sturdy surface not to fall. With or without the top secure, the actual surface of the piece is very slippery. There are ridges, but they do nothing to provide any sort of non-slippery surface. It’s very smooth and slick.

Last, the materials themselves seem okay, but by no means strong enough to last a long time. The pieces that snap in - by virtue they are already not in - seemed like they could snap if we fought to get them in. We did try - they did not snap - but there was no way to do it. They would not snap. Does that mean the material is strong? No, we don’t think so. We think it’s just how it was made - we are still not sure one of the snap pieces even exists - we can’t see it at all.

Overall this is a nice idea, but horrible execution and a bad product. I will not and cannot recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Gold's Gym XR 5.9 Weight Bench And that was just putting this bench together. Was given one of these as a Christmas present. But it was still in the box - so it had to assembled. From start to finish this took me more than an hour to do, and I built up a sweat doing it. This review is more about that experience as I haven't had the bench put together long enough to comment on how well it works for regular exercise.

First off, the model I got is a bit different than the one show in the photo on this product page. It's very similar, which leads me to think that there have been some recent design changes. The main differences I see comparing the photo to the one I got is that the two bars that rest on the floor are separate items that now attach with bolts instead of being welded. The only other thing I notice is that the pads on my bench are a solid color material, and not two -toned. There may be other differences but given the limited amount that I can see from the photo, that is all I can comment on.

You are going to need some tools to put this bench together. Number one on that list would be an [[ASIN:B000NIK9S2 adjustable wrench]] - you could probably use a socket wrench it you have a set. You also need at least a [[ASIN:B000NNFSKG wide mouth pliers]] - again you could use another adjustable wrench if you had one or even some regular slip-joint pliers. There are a lot of bolts & nuts that go into the assembly of this bench that need to be tightened. You're also going to need a philips-head screw driver. And in my case, I also needed a rat-tail file and a regular metal file.

Opening the box I was confronted with a lot of parts and pieces. Luckily the instruction were on top of all of that. Reading through them I found them pretty easy to understand and with the illustrations it was simple to follow the directions. All the hardware (nuts, bolts, washers, screws, and grease packet) was vacuum sealed to a piece of cardboard and everything was plainly labeled so that matching the right part to the directions was really easy. But be sure to read through the instructions before starting the assembly.

I found the bench fairly easy to assemble - but then I have had some previous experiences with doing this kind of thing. I would imagine some people might find the process a bit overwhelming. I did have one major hiccup. Step 5 has you connect the two parts of the frame (the bar that runs the length of the bench) together with two bolts. One piece of the frame slides into the other and you are suppose to line up to holes on one with the screw threads on the other. My pieces didn't line up. The holes didn't exactly match, so I could not get the bolts to screw in. I spent a half-hour with a rat-tail file trying to make one side of the holes larger, and then I got the bright idea to simply file down the end of the frame itself. That worked. If I hadn't been able to do that I would have had to return the bench and get a replacement. Once past that hurdle the rest of the bench was a snap to put together. I did think I had some 'spare parts' as I had a single nut and bolt left over when I was done - but reading through the directions again I found that I had missed putting those on the tip of the pivot bracket.

Now all I have to do is find the floor space to put this and time to use it. I'm giving this four-stars mainly due to the issue with the frame. I probably should give it an even lower rating because of that, but now that I have it all together it does look to be a decent piece of exercise equipment. I may later come back and update my review to comment on the use I'm getting out of it.

Review for Gold's Gym XR 5.9, model no. GCBE4869.8
text_fidelity_b: Gold's Gym XR 5.9 Weight Bench

Didn't see me although I was right in front of him with my arm out, signaling for 30 seconds before I attempted my turn. text_fidelity_a:
Intex Prestige Downy Airbed Kit with Hand Held Battery Pump, Twin First, it should be understood that these airbeds are not made to last all that long, even if used only inside a house. The periphery seams may separate, the plastic membrane is easily punctured, the ribbing may come unglued, the valve may develop a leak, etc. I use them in lieu of a regular mattress on my bed, with a smooth bedspring below, so nothing sharp around, very little dynamic stress (I don't bounce on the bed ;-), yet none has lasted longer than 2 years. Of course, that's for being in use every single night, not just for an occasional camping trip; it still makes them way cheaper than any "real" mattress.
I have tried several brands available on Amazon and locally; almost all died within a month or two, but the Intex ones all lasted 9-20 months. No punctures, no leaks, but they finally failed by losing their ribbing -- a rib comes loose, creating a big bubble of air; you can lose one rib and still do fine if it was on the side, but by the time you've lost two ribs, it's getting hard to use ;-)
Since none has ever leaked, no valve has ever failed, and we've never had a puncture (over 10 years of use of the Intex model), I suspect that, if Intex could (or wanted to) strengthen the attachment of these internal ribs, this would become a lifetime mattress. Perhaps their business model cannot accommodate such long life...
Since we use two of these and have to replace them every couple of years, we have accumulated quite a supply of these silly battery-powered inflation pumps (originally 8 D-cells, now 6 C-cells). They all still work, but we really need only one since the mattresses never leak. Thus it would be much better if the pump was sold separately -- as it is, it's a conspicuous waste of resources.
text_fidelity_b: Intex Prestige Downy Airbed Kit with Hand Held Battery Pump, Twin

LifeSpan TR1200i Folding Treadmill A four star rating. I have to qualify that. If all I want is a standalone machine to work out on, this is a five star machine. But, the Fitness Club and computerized system - junk as far as I have figure it out.

I delayed reviewing for two years to make sure I could do a good review.

For walking or running, it is smooth and reliable. I like the many different workout profiles shifting speed and incline and they stand the test of time. If that is all you want, buy this machine.

But, they ship it without a USB storage device when using USB is supposed to be central to using the Fitness Club and better managing your workout and physical fitness.

So I bought a USB stick and followed instructions. The machine has never uploaded a workout to the stick following all the instructions. And frankly, that makes this machine worthless for fitness management. The interactivehealthpartner website would be a good tool if I could just get the link between machine and computer to work. Several calls to the company and I got the idiot treatment.

So, summary, I can't recommend or not recommend this machine. I assume there is an included cost for the membership and electronic brains of this machine and membership. Thus, for just a machine I would look for something cheaper. For a machine with all the bells and whistles, I'd buy something else that really works and at least includes a 5 dollar USB stick!
text_fidelity_b: LifeSpan TR1200i Folding Treadmill

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness Space Efficient Multi-Function Magnetic Rowing Machine We took delivery three weeks ago. Relatively easy to set up, but be aware that the seat likes to slide to the end of the stops. Now that we are used to it, my wife and I use it every day, sometimes multiple times a day. We don't put it away, just leave it in place next to the wall, facing the TV.
My main issue is that it, like all the other rowers I've seen, sits too low for someone who (like me) is 76 and 250lbs, with bad knees. At first, I'd either fall the last three inches, hopefully onto the seat, or need some sort of support to get on and off. I solved that problem by wrapping an old belt around the body (see pic), which I could use as a grab bar to lower myself on and lift myself off. If Sunny would put a grab handle on the front, that would be a big help, and save on belts.
A secondary issue is the LCD display. Others have complained that it's not bright enough. The real problem is that it's at the wrong angle. I repurposed a chunk of plastic foam packing to lift the bottom enough to make it clearly visible when seated. Sunny could duplicate that with a simple folding frame.
I should also note that the labeling on the display is wrong. Label says: Time, Count, Total Count, Calories. Actual is: Time, Count, Calories, Total Count.
Finally, I note that almost all of the self-help videos on rowing emphasize managing your strokes per minute. The display doesn't show that. I'd be willing to give up both Total Count and Calories to get that in the display. After all, Total Count is only useful if you are the only person using the machine, and Calories are pretty much a meaningless guess without information like body weight.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Space Efficient Multi-Function Magnetic Rowing Machine

text_fidelity_a:
H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults My wife and I have wanted to get on the water with SUPs or kayaks since trying them on a tour a few years ago, however, unable to have any storage at home, we have been unable to. Then we saw inflatable SUPs and thought we’d be able to give that a try. I had the opportunity to get this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and I jumped! Of course, we live in a hot weather state with summer rainy (storm) season and I’ve had major surgery this year with a longer recovery, so unfortunately we have not yet been able to get onto the water. But as the weather calms and I’ve been cleared... we’ll be out there sooner than later. In the mean time, we finally had a chance to blow up this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and so far so good - we are sure this is going to turn out to be a great thing for us! This H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board comes with several items to get you going (able cuff, repair kit, pump), but do not forget, you’ll want to have some sort of safety vest (required by law in our state - NOT INCLUDED in this kit).

The pump to get it inflated is included and for us, worked pretty well. We took turns to pump it up and while it took some time (and strength we’re both currently lacking post surgery and injury) we were still able to get it “almost fully inflated.” I say “almost” because the company recommended 15 PSI and we only got to 10. That 15 is for “optimal use” and no higher. We felt like the 10 would be good, but when we are out there (and I have more energy back) we will go a bit higher than the 10 As you can see in the pics, it is very inflated and looks good, my wife able too and on it and feel firm and secure. Standing on it she said it felt like (on water) it’ll have good, solid balance and allow a feeling of security on the water. This SUP looks and feels “narrow and long” to us based on our experiences on tours, but something we both would feel comfortable on. We will update this review once we can get out there. In the mean time, we are really happy with this SUP and how easily it went together. Or blown into shape. The removal of air was easy and took only a couple minutes. I’ll say, when she first opened the valve there was a LOUD HIGH PITCHED!!! sound that hurt both our ears, but it went away pretty quickly. Then completed the air removal. My wife did point out the ONE CON is this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board has a VERY pointy and painful value piece you push on - it was not at all comfortable and hurt her finger enough she grabbed a piece of the wrapping it came in to cushion her finger.

We have not used nor opened the paddle that came with. We felt like its weight in the bag was alright, but had a chance to get another that was lighter. We will try both. But we also feel like having two paddles is safest - one with in case something happens to the second.

There are hooks on the deck where you can attach a kayak seat for sitting down - something I prefer. I have weaker ankles from years of sports, so I can tire easily on SUPs. I’ll look forward to this addition - NOT INCLUDED in this kit, but available from H2O as an add-on.

Overall this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board is a great board and we are even more excited to get to our coast and use it. In the mean time, we are very happy with how easy this SUP gets set up and takes down and feel like it’s sturdy and well made enough it’ll be great for a good long time.
text_fidelity_b: H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults

text_fidelity_a:
LEZYNE MTB Specific Micro Floor Drive Pump Read good reviews of the Lezyne Micro Floor Drive HV on [...] and figured I'd give it a try. My previous hand pump was too tiring on the arms when pumping up 2.2" tires on the trail. I needed a small floor pump version to carry with me in my CamelBak on my mountain bike rides. The pump I received weighed in at 210g. The mounting bracket was another 18g which I won't need. With my previous hand pump I could easily fit 2 fingers on each side of the T shaped handle for more grip. The Micro Floor Drive HV handle is quite small and I can only fit 1 finger on each side of the handle which feels awkward, but since I can now use 2 hands to press down it's not too bad. Overall I'm happy with this product, but wish it was a bit smaller in length and width.

Pros:
+ Feels very solid
+ Very nice screw on Presta AND Schrader valve
+ Can use like a floor pump
+ Made for pumping MTB tires, pumps air fast

Cons:
- Longer and wider than a typical hand pump
- Small T shaped handle
- Somewhat heavy, weight 228g (210g pump + 18g mounting bracket)

UPDATE (11/5/2014)
I've been using this pump for almost 4 years now and have had zero problems pumping tires with Presta and Schrader valves. 100 pumps will get a 26 x 2.0 tire to a comfortable pressure (I estimate just below 30 psi). 120 pumps will yield a very firm tire. The foot peg makes pumping a breeze. I've updated the rating from 4 to 5 stars and added measurements below.

Measurements:
Length: 12 1/8 inches from base to top of hose wrapped around the T-handle
Length: 11 3/4 inches from base to top of T-handle
Width: 63.6 mm (2.5") at base
Width: 45.7 mm (1.8") half way from base with hose touching sides of cylinder
Width: 52.8 mm (2.08") at T-handle including hose on both sides
Depth: 30.3 mm (1.2") at base
Depth: 19.8 mm (0.78") at T-handle

text_fidelity_a:
High Sierra Karadon Frame Pack, Amethyst/BlackBerry/Orchid, 30L (S-M) As far as looks go, this backpack is really nice! If a backpack can be called "lovely", I'd have to say that about this one. It's well made and appears very sturdy. It looks to be a high quality backpack.

I think all body types will be different, but for me, this backpack is comfortable to wear. The shoulders and hips have extra padding, so it doesn't rub into those parts. There's plenty of adjustable straps to make it more likely to fit each person just the way they need it to. The padding on the hips and shoulders are also removable, so you can (hand)wash those parts most likely to get sweaty and stinky. I haven't washed these parts yet, but right now they are attached very well. You have to really pull it to get it off, but it's not so hard that you're going to pull a muscle.

There's a rain guard attached within one of the pockets, so you can easily keep the backpack and your belongings dry if it rains. (This is the bottom pocket and the zipper is on the underside of the backpack.) There's extra room in there if you wanted to store anything with the rain guard. The middle space within the backpack is accessed from both the top and the middle, and it is open the whole length of the backpack. It is very roomy, and can be expanded with the 4 adjustable straps on the sides. (2 on each side) There's also a pocket behind the main one. Though it's not as roomy as the middle space, it still gives you lots of extra space. There's a pocket(without zippers or extras) on each side also. Each side of the hip strap has a little zippered pocket and one without a zipper. There's also a zippered pocket on the top cover. There's lots of adjustable straps all around, and also a couple of hooks.

Overall, this is a super nice and comfortable backpack, and I think most ladies will be extremely pleased with it.
text_fidelity_b: High Sierra Karadon Frame Pack, Amethyst/BlackBerry/Orchid, 30L (S-M)

text_fidelity_a: Platypus Platy 2-Liter Flexible Water Bottle For what it is, this is a really nifty vessel for drinking water from. I used it recently for a trip where I wanted to take only one backpack with all of my clothes and gear. While I *probably* could have crammed a water bottle in my bag, this definitely was a defining factor between making my bag too tightly jam-packed and just right. It becomes practically nothing and so lightweight when it's empty. Surprisingly, it stands well on its own when filled and due to the shape and rigidity of the sides, you can pick it up relatively comfortably and tilt it like a normal waterbottle. Of course, you can also only partially fill it, which makes it rather "flat" and slides into a small space on my backpack, which is great. It can make it a little more awkward to drink from. Ultimately, I wouldn't say this is "the best one handed water bottle" and it certainly isn't insulative and it surely can't be the most durable or the easiest to clean. But if you're just looking for a water bottle that can slip away into nothingness but be at the ready, I was more than happy to use this for a week+. Especially for the price. That being said, I was using the 1-litre bottle, which looks to be roughly the same design as the 2 but obviously more standard water bottle scale.
text_fidelity_b: Platypus Platy 2-Liter Flexible Water Bottle

Recommended.

Eazy2hD Rubber Squat Wedge Block (4PCS) for Heel Elevated Squat Adjustable Non-Slip Slant Board for Squat Calf Stretcher Squat Ramp Deadlift Wedge Improve Mobility Balance and Strength We had no idea really what to expect. We'd seen wedges around and tool a look, finding they supposedly help with squats to support and work the legs more. Okay... but is it a gimmick? In the end I grabbed these Eazy2hD Squat Wedge Block (4PCS) for Heel Elevated Squat to find out and my wife and I are thrilled. Okay, we've only used them a couple times, but so far so good and we are feeling a burn - the good kind. We were both athletes in our younger days and are working to get back into peak form, so we are looking for things that support past injuries in GenX bodies while getting into solid physical health. We took a few minutes each to try these and were both surprised by the support we felt in our knees, hamstrings, and overall legs.

The Eazy2hD Squat Wedge Block (4PCS) for Heel Elevated Squat arrive in a bag - the one you carry them in - inside another bag. This caught us off guard - not the bag, but that whatever was in this bag (we had a few things arriving that day) was SO heavy. What could it be... opened the one to reveal the other and... they're wedges. Wow. We were blown away by the weight, but then talked about it and not having thought about it, realized this would increase safety as you stand and squat down onto these things. Okay, so heavy, check. But substantial, check. Opened the carrying bag - which is a great bonus - keep them together and carry them from room to room, store them in our workout box, whatever, they are well kept. Nice bag.

So pulled them out - there are two, each two pieces. This allows you to adjust the height and such. Now I love to do clay stretching this way - goes back to soccer, baseball, and track days. I was able to get some good stretching here, which is helping me heal a torn hamstring. I felt the burn, but without the pain. I also had pulled another muscle on the same leg that flares every so often, but in doing the squats, I was able to not feel that muscle and it gave me a nice stretch that loosened and warmed up the whole leg.

I have only used them at with the two pieces, not one, so we'll play with them and see. But they did not slip, held their spot on the carpet, and felt great under bare feet - we do both bare and shoed when we workout. There was no discomfort or pain bare footed. But not sure if I'd do longer on them without shoes - no particular reason, just a thought.

We are just starting with these Eazy2hD Squat Wedge Block (4PCS) for Heel Elevated Squat, but so far we are very impressed. If nothing else, the squat is a much "easier" and more comfortable move that feels like we are getting a better workout from than the "old" way of doing it. That alone is worth it to us!
text_fidelity_b: Eazy2hD Rubber Squat Wedge Block (4PCS) for Heel Elevated Squat Adjustable Non-Slip Slant Board for Squat Calf Stretcher Squat Ramp Deadlift Wedge Improve Mobility Balance and Strength

text_fidelity_a:
Razor Beast Kick Scooter Don't mess up and not fully understand the bar height or size of this itty bitty scooter. I guess they think there are a lot of four foot tall 220 pound kids. The product itself is sturdy. I love that it doesn't rattle and the brake is my favorite ever on a Razor scooter. A scooter that handles 220 lbs should have a taller bar imo.

Bought one on a big sale on a total mistake because I didn't understand the bar is only 17 inches. Hassle to return it so I plan on just leaving it in my car all the time as an Emergency scooter because if you are over 5 feet tall it will not be anything you can actually use regularly. It is not worth 90 dollars or the 30 I paid for anyone over 5 feet. It doesn't rattle and it has a great brake. That's it. A small child should enjoy a Razor that doesn't rattle and it seems nice quality. The different sites or places that say this is 8 to adult 220 lb weight limit don't tell ya the bar height will be a little above your knees a little if you are 5'10".

The A5 Lux (which rattles but is adult human size) pictured with it shows how tiny the Beast is and the bar height I actually need and use. Beast. More like a Mini....mouse. I admit my mistake in not researching this better and thinking I was getting a great deal but this thing is tiny. Tiny.
text_fidelity_b: Razor Beast Kick Scooter

text_fidelity_a:
Monstrum Tactical MOLLE Utility Pouch Here I am again, this time I'm looking for the best pouch possible for a very specific carry option. I've wanted something to carry one of my home made mini EDC kits, plus a few other items. I've found some really nice models, but they were usually too big or too small. Some were a great size for my needs, but were cost prohibitive.

Alas, I found a Monstrum Tactical MOLLE Utility Pouch on Amazon for about $14. I had narrowed it down to this item over a Condor Gadget MOLLE Pouch. The prices were nearly identical, so I went over both items with a discerning eye. The Monstrum was about a half-inch smaller, so it was a close call.

I believe some Monstrum products mimic their higher priced competition, yet still make a great value. There may be subtle differences here and there, but there were no major must-haves. I rarely go for the high end products when I find one that is similar for a lower price and good reviews. A quick note on reviews? Take them ALL with a grain of salt.

The Monstrum pouch appears to be very well made. The stitching appears sturdy and I only found one loose thread, which I burned down in about 3 seconds. It was a small detail, but it lent itself to the overall quality. The zippers, zipper pulls, and Velcro patches are also solid.

Features on the pouch were way more than I expected and what I saw online. As I looked it over, right after opening the Amazon box, I knew I had hit a homerun. From the front, there is a hard pouch cover with a zippered pocket. On the underside of that cover is a heavy duty patch of Velcro that connects to the front, expandable, pocket. On either side of that pocket are elastic loops that can be adjusted to hold the pocket tightly closed. In this front area, you have it subdivided into different sections. Behind this front area, you have the main pocket. It has 3 subdivisions and they held everything I wanted with a tiny bit of room left. This main pocket has two zippers w/pulls. On the back of the pouch, there are two MOLLE snap straps, which are useful to wear on a belt, if you know how to weave them correctly.

One of the main things that I liked was the expandable front pocket. It really protrudes as you add more stuff, so those adjustable elastic straps help it stay secure. It more than serves its purpose.

Pros:
Cost @ $14
Strong & sturdy
Perfect size for a mini-EDC kit and other small items
Multiple carry options

Cons:
It looks pregnant with all the stuff I put in there, so that's a bit odd.
(As was that statement).

Final verdict? Take a close look for yourself on the Monstrum or Amazon websites and see for yourself. If you have a couple of handfuls of small-ish gear you want to keep in its own pouch, this may work out perfect for you too.
text_fidelity_b: Monstrum Tactical MOLLE Utility Pouch

Wilson Pro Overgrip (12 Pack) If you get this with free super saver shipping, this works out to be about $1 per wrap. That's quite a deal for some very nice wraps that work and last.

I use these on my racquetball handle but it will work great on any racquet. The grip level is perfect -- just enough so that the racquet does not twist in your hand and not too much so that switching grips between forehand and backhand is not impeded.

The grip is super easy to install and have the little 'extras' to make it simple. For example:

1) The grips come with a clear saran-wrap coating on one side that you need to peel off before wrapping it around your racquet.

2) The wrap comes with one end cut at an angle so that you get a proper wrap angle.

3) The tip also has a piece of double-sided tape stuck to it to keep it in place while you start wrapping.

4) It comes with a pre-cut piece of tape to finish taping the final end to the racket.

The wrap is also not too thin nor too thick. I did remove the original, factory wrap on my racquet before I put this on.

It also seems to have a very nice wear level. I have played 4 weeks now (3 games a week) and have no wear holes.
text_fidelity_b: Wilson Pro Overgrip (12 Pack)

text_fidelity_a:
TETON Sports Outfitter XXL Camping Cot; Camping Cots for Adults; Folding Cot Bed; Easy Set Up; Storage Bag Included If you are familiar with a folding Army cot, then you know this cot. It’s essentially the same thing in a larger format. I was going to say in a larger, heavier-duty format, but that’s not entirely true. The Army cots have a couple of advantages over this one. However, this cot is pretty nice and HUGE, and kind of heavy. It’s hard to appreciate how big it is until you set it up. That’s really the main disadvantage I have with it, but it’s also the exact reason I bought it.

It comes with a pretty heavy duty carry bag with is unique. It doesn’t zip closed, but instead had a couple of Velcro loops to close it. Sort of like a shopping bag with Velcro. It works and should stand up to some abuse from camping.

The only issue I have with it, as other reviewers have commented, is the end pieces will pop off if you use them to move the cot. Get used to just not ever touching them, or else they’ll pop off and you have to struggle through getting them back on. This is where the design of an Army cot has an advantage: they don’t pop out because of how it’s designed. But, I’m sure the Teton cot won’t fall apart in the middle of the night, so it’s a minor point.
text_fidelity_b: TETON Sports Outfitter XXL Camping Cot; Camping Cots for Adults; Folding Cot Bed; Easy Set Up; Storage Bag Included

text_fidelity_a:
Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire I purchased Campy Shamal 2-way rims a couple years back. I then purchased everything needed to mount and maintain tubeless tires including Fusion 3s. I ride a '12 Specialized S-Works Roubaix and mostly do fast training rides about 3 to 4 days a week with longer rides beyond 60 miles fairly regularly. I weigh out at roughly 185 pounds.

Tubeless and ceramic bearings are somewhat in the same category these days in terms of bikers wondering if this equipment truly makes a difference. Well, I've ridden ceramic bearings in my crank and in my wheels...and YES...it makes a difference...now...I've ridden on tubeless for two riding seasons...and YES...they make a difference. Tubeless is the future...as it is in nearly every vehicle that has wheels from a riding mower to a motorcycle to a car...and mountain bikes. Why it has taken so long with road biking is understandable...change is hard...and manufacturers will go where the money is.

First, let me make this clear...putting the Fusion 3 tires on was a chore...and I mean...a CHORE. It will test your patience. Do NOT succumb to using levers as it will ruin the bead. Google tubeless tire installation for help but even then it will baffle you as to how you're going to get that tire over the rim...but...you will...and the benefits will be worth it.

Second, it takes a few rides to get the tires truly seated. Use an air compressed pump if you've got it...but...I had a "Joe Blow" floor pump that worked fine. I didn't install the sealant until after the second short ride and pump up. You will most likely lose quite a bit of air at first but as the tire seals over time...the air pressure stabilized. I do pump up my tires before every ride but it isn't out of the norm of my former clincher tires.

Third, I've ridden my fusion 3s at 90psi on the front tire and 100psi on the back. The ride is fast & super smooth. A lot of riders think super high psi is better but that is, (arguably for some), not true because at a high psi your tire is actually bumping up and down off the road which drains energy transfer over time. The benefit of running tubeless at lower psi is that the tire remains in more constant contact with the road which...over time...equals better energy transfer...and hence...speed, comfort, and endurance. Also, there is some evidence that without a tube you eliminate friction...I'm honestly not sure about that claim...even so, I can say from experience that I'm not going back to tubed tires...tubeless tires run as advertised.

Fourth, durability...I run typical roads here in Maryland over countless miles...up and down hills...less maintained side roads...and these Fusion 3s can go yet another season. The wear is normal with no unusual issues. I've NOT had one flat tire. I've NOT added more sealant since the first install...which I should've done...but...it hasn't made a difference.

Fifth, the only reservation I have is getting a flat tire but I guess it's a good thing that I'm not as use to dealing with flats like I had for my tubed tires. I have to say it has been a pleasure to not have had one flat for two seasons.

I'd like to try the ATOM version of this tire...and I think I'll get it just for comparison purposes. Not looking forward to the install and my expectation is that they will not fit my riding style, endurance expectations, and my higher weight...even so, I'm a believer in trying anything once...so...we'll see.

All in all...educate yourself but don't be afraid to go tubeless. It is change that we all seem to avoid but I'll never go back now that I've tried it out...and as the biking money goes...tubeless quality and selection will as well. ENJOY!
text_fidelity_b: Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire

text_fidelity_a:
Flasite Hoola-Hoop-Weighted-for-Adults-and-Kids - Weight Loss Pilates Trainer Circle 27 Sections Detachable Knots Fitness& Massage Abdomen Exercise Hoops I've been using this for about two weeks now. It does what I bought it to do and I have a lot of fun using it, but there are certain flaws that lead me to say it's overpriced.

First the good: it's easy to put together and works as advertised. It took me a few tries to find the right fit (a little tighter than I first thought) and several practice attempts before I could get the weight spinning long enough for a good workout (but I was never that great at regular hula hoops as a kid). Playing with the length of the cord also resulted in a much better workout, and the catch is very strong; it holds whatever length I set no matter how hard or long I use it.

Snapping the links into position was moderately challenging, but my grip strength is relatively poor so no surprise there. Opening and closing the hoop for actual use is easy, and that's what's important. There's a novelty factor to this, of course, but I do find it fun to use, which motivates me to use it regularly.

Now the not so good: a few of the pieces arrived broken. Although I don't need those links now, it's disappointing that I won't have them in the future if need be.

A bigger issue is that this thing is loud -- not "wake the neighbors" loud but loud enough to disturb others in the house. I wasn't expecting it to be utterly silent, but neither was I expecting this rattling. This limits my use of it somewhat.

I got this as a cardio option other than walking or biking. I have posterior tibial tendonitis -- a fancy way of saying tendonitis of the ankle/foot; walking or running for long distances can irritate it, and biking isn't always an option for me. The weighted hula hoop is a very good alternative to these activities because I can get a good cardio workout without aggravating my PTT. Admittedly, I can't go as long with this as I can walking or biking, but I can make it a lot more intense. Besides, this is still kind of new to me, and I'm confident that I can build my stamina over time. Judging from the feel of the materials, though, I'm not sure how durable this device will be.

Prices here vary all the time, of course. I got this for about $35 altogether. Given the breakage, I'd say that was slightly overpriced; I certainly wouldn't advise anyone to pay more than that for this. It's a nice tool for your home gym, but I'd wait to buy it on sale or at least until February when most of us have left our new year's resolutions in the dust.
text_fidelity_b: Flasite Hoola-Hoop-Weighted-for-Adults-and-Kids - Weight Loss Pilates Trainer Circle 27 Sections Detachable Knots Fitness& Massage Abdomen Exercise Hoops

text_fidelity_a:
Electric Battery Operated Heated Socks Men Women Rechargeable Washable for Hunting Winter Skiing Mobile Warming Powered Battery Heated Socks… I had high hopes for these electric socks. I mean, electric blankets have been around forever, right? So maybe, just maybe these would work. Sadly, they are utter crap.

When they arrived, they didn't look too bad. I was concerned about how much of the sock would have a heated area, but I figured, even a relatively small area might be helpful. I got some fresh AA batteries and loaded up the battery compartments. (There is a little pocket near the top outer side of each sock. There is a wire inside each of these that connects to the battery box.)

I felt just the faintest bit of warmth from one sock and nothing from the other. I put them on and honestly could not tell a difference between the non-working side and the one that was faintly warm. I thought perhaps they needed more time to warm up, so I continued wearing them hoping that would happen. I was busy working and after a couple of hours realized that they had never warmed up. So I decided to check the batteries, 'just in case,' they weren't fully charged. When I checked them on my battery tester, all four were completely dead even though I had gotten them from my fresh supply. I wondered if they could possibly have been bad to begin with, though that seemed highly unlikely. Then I wondered if the box had somehow drained the batteries.

Still holding out a tiny bit of hope the socks would warm, I got out more batteries. This time I checked them with my battery tester first, to make sure they were fully charged. They were. Again I felt the tiniest bit of warmth and thought, "Great! I guess the last batch of batteries were no good."

Put them on and again, could not feel the warmth. I later checked the fully charged batteries and .. you guessed it, they were drained. So not only did the stupid socks not work, they somehow drained EIGHT AA batteries!! What a waste of time and money. Needless to say, I want to send these back.

It's really a shame because a lot of people would love to have socks like this if they would actually work. I hope the manufacturer figures out a way to make them work AND do so without having to go through dozens of batteries each week.
text_fidelity_b: Electric Battery Operated Heated Socks Men Women Rechargeable Washable for Hunting Winter Skiing Mobile Warming Powered Battery Heated Socks…

text_fidelity_a:
Alloy Car Roof Bike Bicycle Fork Mount Carrier Rack Max Load 44 lbs After reading the pros and cons of fork-mounting vs upright (wheel-mount) I decided to go with these, figuring the mostly aluminum structure would last a while and the fork-mounting would secure the bikes well. I've used the product one time on a short trip, but so far it seems sturdy and the bikes are locked on firmly. My one concern, which I knew in advance of purchase, is that the fork mount only holds the traditional thin skewers/axles. That works fine for our family fleet of tourers and hybrids from years 1998 through about 2012. However, a lot of new bikes now have the much fatter through-axles (particularly bikes w/ disc brakes). So if i get a new bike I'll probably need a new rack.

Vehicle: 2016 Subaru Outback

Pros:
-My big Cannondale Adventure 400 and my wife's Giant Sedona fit perfectly and are secured with front quick release and included rear hold-down strap.
-Reasonable price, though not as inexpensive as some all-steel models out there.
-No tools required, no customization needed for our Outback with factory folding roof rack.
-Seems and looks solid for those worried about appearance.

Cons:
-May need to fiddle with how many spacers to use with each bolt. There are six bolts on each rack.
-Installation, certainly the first time, might take up to 20 minutes for each rack. And sometimes it's hard to get those big wingnuts to thread properly given the awkward angle since the bolt is vertical and you may not have much space to install the wingnut between bolt and roof of car.
-Very easy to have the spacers fall off the bolts before wingnut is threaded. I had two or three roll off the back of our vehicle. No biggie on a flat concrete driveway but can be a problem on gravel or camping.
-It doesn't lock, which is okay for our needs. I can probably run a cable lock through the frame/tires and part of our roof rack. This may not keep the racks from being stolen but it would be a real pain to remove with bikes mounted. -Of course, it's nice to leave the rack on all summer if you use it frequently, but note someone can get a rack off in 3 minutes if there's no bike on it.
-For any roof rack, it may take a little strength and height to put the bike on top of a car/SUV and simultaneously align that front fork with the locking axle (built into the rack). I'm over 6 feet but my wife is 5'-6" - no way can she use this rack w/ her hybrid. Might be different w/ an ultra-light tourer and a foot stool.
text_fidelity_b: Alloy Car Roof Bike Bicycle Fork Mount Carrier Rack Max Load 44 lbs

text_fidelity_a: YICFIS Upgraded LED Reflective Vest Running Gear, USB Rechargeable Running Gear Night Light up Vest Safety Gear Adjustable Size for Runners Walkers Men Women… We do a lot of night walks with our 2 dogs and there is a fair amount of traffic in our neighborhood, so we try to make ourselves as visible as possible. We've tried other light up vests but found some do not adjust well for taller/larger people. This one is great! It has quite a bit of room to adjust for both height and breadth, and easy to make that adjustment. It has 2 orange lights - similar in size to one of the thick glow sticks. One is on the front, one is on the back. It buckles around the waist with a button that slides/locks into a hole. There are 3 connection points - 2 on the waist (from either side of the waist strap) and one from the strip coming down from your chest to your waist. They all connect in to the small pouch on the front. You really only need to undo one once you get it sized to the settings you want. The small pouch is great for holding your phone, keys or poop bags. The lights are very bright and can easily be seen from a good distance away. Love the fact that it is rechargeable and don't need to mess with batteries. We are very happy with this vest and may end up ordering another one!
text_fidelity_b: YICFIS Upgraded LED Reflective Vest Running Gear, USB Rechargeable Running Gear Night Light up Vest Safety Gear Adjustable Size for Runners Walkers Men Women…

Bottle with Carry Cap Garbage. Garbage. Wait....nope definitely garbage sums it up.

I bought this piece of garbage for probably one of the dumbest reasons ever...I got the refill filters on clearance at Target. Like I couldn't resist ridiculously cheap I should have known better since they were so cheap cheap. So since I had all these filters and no bottle I had to get the bottle. Boy did I go wrong...

I've attached pictures of the warped bottle. The brand name Bobble clearly reflects the transition it has undergone to get to its current warped stage. By warped I mean it no longer is able to sit in an upright position and has a permanent gangsta lean going. Needless to say I was PO'd and contacted the seller (who was AAA+++ by the way so kudos to them for their superb customer service). Fortunately I got a refund on this bad investment. The saddest part (of course aside from me buying the refills because they were on clearance) was that this was purchased for my 7 year old son who thought this Bobble was like the coolest looking water bottle ever. He even accepted it in its obviously imperfectly warped status. He was totally accepting of his Bobble only being able to lay on its side and found it rather funny that it looked really "crooked".....My opinion wasn't as accepting and I sent off a massive complaint letter to the manufacturer of this POS.

Bottomline people- avoid this bad boy Bobble like the plague. This would be why Target clearanced those damn Bobble refills out. Live and learn my friends. Live and learn.
